# Tutorial: hierarchical clustering {#hclust}

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(selectiveHotelling)
```

For hierarchical clustering, set `clustering = "hclust"`. By default the package uses
average linkage on squared Euclidean distances and cuts the tree into `K` clusters;
`hclust_method` chooses another linkage.

```{r hclust-data}
set.seed(123)
Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.6, 0.6, 1), 2, 2)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2), matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) + 4) %*% chol(Sigma)
res <- selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 2, clustering = "hclust", M = 1000)
res
table(res$cluster)
```

The two clusters come from two different groups, and the test rejects. With a single group,
it does not:

```{r hclust-null}
set.seed(321)
X0 <- matrix(rnorm(200), ncol = 2) %*% chol(Sigma)
res0 <- selective_hotelling_test(X0, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 2, clustering = "hclust",
                                 M = 1000)
res0$pval
```

With complete linkage:

```{r hclust-complete}
selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 2, clustering = "hclust",
                         hclust_method = "complete", M = 1000)$pval
```

Average-linkage hierarchical clustering is sensitive to outliers. Chapter \@ref(details)
discusses when the tests rely on Gaussian data.
